affiliations.date_precision: The Aspen Times profile says Caudill entered Cornell in fall 1940 and that wartime service interrupted his schooling. Cornell records associate him with the Class of 1944 and a 1946 architecture degree; no exact interruption date is supplied.
affiliations.research_notes: Cornell is a documented prewar student affiliation and the last identified civilian status before wartime service. It is not an employer and is not the immediate pre-OSS affiliation because the source documents intervening Army cavalry-school training.

affiliations.organization_name_as_found: the cavalry school in Fort Riley
affiliations.date_precision: The Aspen Times profile places a short cavalry-school stint after Cornell and before service as an Army OSS second lieutenant, but supplies no dates or formal unit designation.
affiliations.research_notes: The source supplies a direct sequence but not a service record. Publish as the best-supported probable immediate military training assignment, visibly qualified and not counted as a civilian employer.

claims.claim_text: An official history identifies an OSS Sergeant Steve J. Catlos, but the private identifier printed in the index resolves to a different official Army subject, so the indexed identity remains conflicting.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact uncommon name appears in an official OSS history, while exact private-identifier comparison connects the index row to a different Army name.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Conflicting. The uncommon name and OSS context strongly support the historical candidate, but the official identifier disagreement prevents a settled link.
claims.temporal_assessment: The NPS narrative documents an OSS assignment in the Budapest-Slovakia mission; the conflicting Army record cannot establish Catlos's pre-OSS chronology.
claims.match_notes: Neither full identifier nor the unrelated Army subject is public. No Army occupation, residence, entry, or education facts are assigned to Catlos. Review Box 113 and the original service record.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Samuel J. Caudill is a high-confidence match to architect Samuel Jefferson Caudill Jr., who served as a U.S. Army OSS second lieutenant.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A dated Aspen Times profile supplies the rare full name, Cornell chronology, Army OSS service, rank, and China mission; Cornell independently corroborates name and education.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence. The exact uncommon name, middle initial, OSS service, wartime chronology, and Cornell institutional record align. The index's short printed identifier cannot independently confirm the match.
claims.temporal_assessment: The profile places Cornell study before cavalry-school training and Army OSS service, but provides no exact accession date.
claims.match_notes: High-confidence, not confirmed. The index row's original short identifier remains private and is not treated as a complete Army match.

claims.claim_text: Samuel J. Caudill entered Cornell University as a student in fall 1940, before wartime service interrupted his studies.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Caudill went on to Cornell University in the fall of 1940.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The Aspen Times profile dates Cornell entry and says wartime service interrupted school; Cornell's institutional notice corroborates his class and architecture degree.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The rare full-name OSS biography and Cornell's matching name, class, and degree support the high-confidence person match.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar student status. Intervening Army cavalry-school training means Cornell is not labeled the immediate pre-OSS affiliation.
